quest.title: An Eye for an Eye
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, do you see any walls? I don't see a wall anywhere around here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Walls? There are no walls here.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Then, are the walls somewhere really far away? Cater once told me that if they're too far away to see with your eyes, they'll look like the "horizon."

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, where are we?

choices.text: By the water.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: The water here is lying flat, and there's no walls to separate it from us...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Hm... That thing up in the sky must be the "moon," right? If it were the "sun," it would probably hurt my eyes like the evil sorcerers' magic.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: #All around me are things I've never seen before... and things I've only seen in books! {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, let's go on another adventure!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Cater was right! Adventuring outside is way more fun than in Meropide!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's right. The world outside is vast.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: I really envy the two of you...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Lanoire, let's discuss adventuring later. We really should find your family first...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Freeze, all of you! Where do you think you're going? Also, what's with that little girl?

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Th—The evil sorcerer found us!

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: What business is it of yours? Weren't you on leave? Patrolling with a Gardemek in your off hours won't get you promoted, you know.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: I came back as soon as I received the report... Have you gotten yourself mixed up with them? You're making a grave mistake, Estienne.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Actually, I think you'll find that I'm rectifying a mistake... and saving everyone a lot of paperwork. Ms. Monglane might even invite me to dinner as thanks.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: No... No! They're... criminals! Even if the papers with their serial numbers on them are missing, they're still criminals!

choices.text: A little girl like this is a criminal? Are you out of your mind?

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: I'm perfectly sane. Anyone can be a criminal — little girls are no exception.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This guy is scary...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Whatever other plans you may have had, I must now escort you back to the Fortress of Meropide.

choices.text: How about we go back first and take some time to think it over?

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: You've already dug yourselves a whole lot deeper. When we get back to the Fortress, you'll be held separately and questioned. So, don't get any funny ideas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then there's no way out of this!?

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: I can see quite a few ways, actually. If a few Gardemeks get scrapped in the process, well, that's also what happens when people break the rules.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: It would seem you have no intention of repenting. Then you leave me no choice. Gardemeks show no mercy to recalcitrant criminals.

choices.text: We only just got out, and now you wanna make us go back? I don't think so!

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: You don't have a choice in the matter. You must comply with the rules and accept your punishment.

choices.text: We've been wrongly accused!

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: If you have objections regarding your verdicts, then you must go through the appeals process. But until your charges are overturned, you're all still criminals.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's completely ridiculous!

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Those are the rules that everyone must abide by.

choices.text: We're in Fontaine.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Fontaine... It's a blue and green place. The Fortress of Meropide is all yellow and gray.

choices.text: We're on the continent of Teyvat.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: The continent of Teyvat... Is it just like the Fortress of Meropide? I can't see its walls anywhere, that must make it a really, really big Fortress, right?

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Good heavens! I'm your colleague, you're not thinking of taking me in too?

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: Since you've thrown your lot in with them, you deserve the same punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #Cater... {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon... *sob*...

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: Gardemeks simply get scrapped, but you... Even if you are monsters, you can still feel pain, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is... Is this Hilichurl really Caterpillar? Paimon can't wrap her head around this...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Ms. Paimon, how do you not recognize him? That's Cater...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm... I'm a monster in human skin.

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: A monster... I never imagined such a monster even existed in the Fortress... A Hilichurl that can talk! Who would have thought?

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: Heh, how did you manage to pull the wool over everyone's eyes?

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: What sorcery could allow a mindless creature to worm its way into our midst like a wolf in sheep's clothing...

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: Why haven't you run away yet? Are you pretending to be human? Of course, I will catch you even if you do run.

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: A dangerous monster like you...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm guilty. But she hasn't done anything wrong. She shouldn't be here.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: You won't find her name on any sentencing documents, she is innocent. She only ended up stuck in the Fortress due to a few mishaps.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'll return to the Fortress with you, but have Estienne take her back home.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Cater...

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: The monster actually wants to make a deal with me?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I do indeed. Let her go home. As far as the Fortress of Meropide is concerned, she never existed in the first place. Her absence will not be felt.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But catching a monster like me should be a big deal, no? Fontaine hasn't seen a monster like me for several centuries now...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If you pass up this opportunity, I'll put my human skin back on and slip away into the crowd... You'll never get a chance like this again.

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: You're right. I've never seen her in the Fortress before, she's completely irrelevant.

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: But you... You're too dangerous. I can't risk... letting an evil monster like you get away...

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: We have a deal. You'll return to the Fortress of Meropide, and the girl can leave.

choices.text: It would achieve your goal, might as well take it.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The guilty return to where they should be, and Lanoire returns to her family's side. Everything on the right track, as it should be.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: He is someone who follows the rules. This is also in accordance with the rules.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Enough, monster, I've caught you now. You're all coming back to the Fortress of Meropide with me — the girl included.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? But didn't you just...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Who would actually make a deal with a monster? Could anyone be sure that the words coming out of his mouth aren't some beguiling incantation to stunt human wisdom?

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: I won't be fooled again, so I've decided to play by my own rules. Your documents are missing? Then you'll stay in the Fortress of Meropide for the rest of your lives.

choices.text: You have no right to bypass a trial.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: If you want to emphasize that in your written appeal, be my guest. But until then, you don't have a choice.

choices.text: I surrender.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: A wise decision. I'll make a note of that in your appeal.

choices.text: Don't take the deal, it could be a trick...

dialogues.speaker: Monglane
dialogues.text: ...Welcome back.

dialogues.speaker: Monglane
dialogues.text: Noailles filled appeal forms out for you already. But you should stay out of trouble until a final decision has been made.

dialogues.speaker: Monglane
dialogues.text: More specifically, do not rile him up.

dialogues.speaker: Monglane
dialogues.text: I thought I was getting a coworker who knew what he's doing, so I could be less stressed. But as it turns out, I've only gotten busier since he arrived..

dialogues.speaker: Monglane
dialogues.text: I really want to take a vacation in Natlan.

choices.text: I want to go to Natlan too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, this is not the time for chit-chat! Paimon is wondering how Lanoire and the others are doing...

response.speaker: Monglane
response.text: They're being kept under strict watch now. If you don't want the same treatment, then follow the rules.

choices.text: What happened to them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's you!

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Indeed, it's me!

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Noailles would probably call it "atoning for my sins." But I've got seniority, so he doesn't get to order me around.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then what are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Atoning for my sins, what else?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why does Paimon get the feeling you aren't the least bit surprised? Did you already know Caterpillar's, um... do you know his true identity?

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: I only knew that he'd been here a long time. Longer than any of us.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: As for the rest, is any of it really important? He looks like a human, and he talks like one, too. What can I say? I like chatting with him.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Maybe appearances matter more to me than what's inside.

choices.text: That's understandable.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: In any case, if you're looking for Caterpillar, he's inside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about Lanoire? Is she in there with him?

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: She was taken to go fill in some registration form. But don't worry, she'll be back soon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, then let's ask Caterpillar... Just what's going on with him...

choices.text: I beg to differ.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm sorry for dragging you two into this. My plan was to get Lanoire home to her family, then return on my own. But it looks like that plan was a complete failure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's a lot I want to ask you.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I imagine so.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... You really are Caterpillar, right?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I am.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, um, you're a Hilichurl?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I am.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But.... aren't Hilichurls all, um, kinda dumb? And you looked just like a regular kid before. Ugh... Paimon doesn't know what's real anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You said before that you looked like this because you got sick, after all, everyone has things they'd rather not tell anyone... And you're also so good to Lanoire, and she trusts you too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you're not a human at all... If you're a Hilichurl...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Then you can't trust me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I want the answers to the questions Noailles asked before.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'll answer all your questions truthfully.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: When did you come to the Fortress of Meropide?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Over 400 years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: F—Four hundred years ago!? When you said you'd been here a long time, Paimon thought you meant something like three to five years...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But 400 years is, like, several generations, isn't it? Oh, right... You're a Hilichurl...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What was your crime?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If you're interested in history... I was a member of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. I was found guilty of being an accessory to the master's scheme.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The prophecy of the apocalypse... My master believed that he could stop this future of destruction from coming to pass. We did much to prepare for this. It was a powerful magic, and also an evil plan...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But perhaps none of this is important now. The plan failed, and the Narzissenkreuz Ordo has essentially ceased to exist. Whether Fontaine is destroyed or not, it no longer has anything to do with me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just who was this master you spoke of?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Narzissenkreuz, a powerful mage. He taught me human speech and granted me memory and intelligence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was there really someone who could do something like that? Hmm... But, your appearance aside, you really do seem like an ordinary human...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Though many details of the past have faded into memory, I remember this very well...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: This was a very, very long time ago. I couldn't change how I appeared to others at will then.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Many humans — some in finery, others in rags, some with curiosity, others with disdain — would all ask similar questions.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: "Can Hilichurls really talk?" "Are Hilichurls really capable of intelligence?"

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: My master raised the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz high. It was a ceremonial sword, so the blade wasn't sharp, but still it glistened in the sunlight.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: "Behold," he said, "even a hideous monster such as this can attain wisdom and redemption through my power as the incarnation of Narzissenkreuz."

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I was one of his creations. And as a testament to Narzissenkreuz's power, I once wielded a blade for the Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But the sacred sword evidently couldn't save my master from a fate of failure and ruin. And the mystical, magical weapon... no longer exists.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: And there will be no more monsters in human skin like me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do you want to help Lanoire?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Because of "compassion"...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Humanity might be unattainable for me, but at the very least, I can imitate it. Just like how I learned to change how I appear to others.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't get it...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you both innately possess kindness and benevolence. Because of this, you don't need to think twice about helping others. You simply do.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If you look at their outcomes alone, plenty of actions are indistinguishable from each other. We all agree that Lanoire shouldn't stay in the Fortress of Meropide and that she should return to her family, so we chose to help her.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Your actions come from an innate benevolence that doesn't require excessive consideration or calculation. For me, however... it is because by doing so, I will be more like a human.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Funny, isn't it? I'll never truly become human, yet I can't stop mimicking human behavior.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's like "atonement"... As far as human law is concerned, I've long since atoned for my sins. But a human... What would a true human do?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: They would never forgive themselves for the mistakes they made, the harm they caused, and the people or things they failed to save...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: So, my sins can never be absolved, and I will forever be my own prisoner.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you plan to do next?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'll bring Lanoire back to her family.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But... Forget about getting out of the Fortress, we can't even get past this door!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I made a promise to her... so I have to fulfill it. She shouldn't stay here any longer, especially not by my side.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The Geode Mine Shaft... It's a dangerous route, but it's feasible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Geode Mine Shaft... That's right, Clynes said that there's an opening there that leads outside...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, the guards asked him to install a locking mechanism like the one at the Rift of Erosion there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He also said something about having prepared a "surprise"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes, there's no way that's anything good! Are you sure you want to go from there? Paimon seems to remember that the research terminal there has to be operated by two people at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Lanoire's so small, Paimon doesn't think she'll be able to operate it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Why don't we help them, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: I do innately possess kindness, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have a few more questions about the Ordo, as well...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I think there are other places better suited to discussing the history of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. Somewhere that isn't the Fortress of Meropide, for example.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then we'll just have to wait until after Lanoire is reunited with her family... Before any of that, we need to think of a way out of here. And we need to meet back up with Lanoire.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Estienne will help us open the door. But there's a limit to how much he can help us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He should be at the entrance, right? Let's go ask him!

choices.text: I'll do it for you, Paimon.

talks.objective: Prepare to leave the Fortress of Meropide

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yep, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Thanks for your help.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not yet, I need a little more time.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Of course.

talks.objective: Prepare to leave the Fortress of Meropide
Use the loudspeaker to draw away the guards
Go to the abandoned production zone without being noticed

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: Ready to leave?

talks.objective: Prepare to leave the Fortress of Meropide
Go to the abandoned production zone without being noticed

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: Ready to leave?

talks.objective: Operate the drive valve to open the passage leading to the Geode Mine Shaft

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: Take care.

talks.objective: Go to the Geode Mine Shaft

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not yet.

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: Stay out of trouble... Though I guess it's a little late to be saying that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the Geode Mine Shaft? Paimon's heard of it before, but it's a little different than she imagined...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Wooow! What pretty rocks! Are all of these gems?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's Arkhium. Arkhium mining operations stopped after the Fontaine Research Institute accident.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Maybe we should keep our distance then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, there really is a research terminal here. Hmm... Is that a note next to it? Could Clynes have left it here? Let's see what it says!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the "surprise" Clynes was talking about...? More like a shock!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm... To activate this research terminal, we'll need a mobile energy storage device. But once we have one, we'll get chased by some sort of flying energy thief...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we'll just have to beat this energy thief in a race!

choices.text: I'd like to go back and give Clynes a beating.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—We can't blame it all on him...

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: There's going to be a race? I'll be rooting for you two!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, let's leave this terminal to Caterpillar and Lanoire. We'll take care of the rest.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I'll keep watch. Be careful.

choices.text: But flying is faster than running...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How can you give up before the race has even started?

talks.objective: Acquire the energy storage device and unlock the research terminal ahead
Acquire the energy storage device and unlock the research terminal ahead
Acquire the energy storage device and unlock the research terminal ahead

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why is it off again?

choices.text: The Fontaine Research Institute's tech really is unreliable...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did it malfunction? At least it won't explode this time... probably.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Maybe someone's catching up to us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sh—Should we go back and take a look then?

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: No need to trouble yourselves, esteemed guests.

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: You're evil, and I represent the side of justice... Even without Gardemeks, I won't let you get away...

response.speaker: Noailles
response.text: Lay down your arms and surrender!

choices.text: Someone sent to catch us?

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Maybe.

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: He's... He's just a monster! Why would you help him? Why would anyone help him?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Cater isn't a monster! Why... Why would you call him that, evil sorcerer...?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Ever since Mother left Meropide, Cater's been really nice to me, he's never lied to me...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: There are other nice people here too... but none of them are as nice as Cater. He tells me all kinds of stories, and listens to mine, too...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: I won't let you call him a monster!

dialogues.speaker: Noailles
dialogues.text: Why? Justice should triumph over evil...

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: There's no such thing as good or evil here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Estienne! What are you doing here?

choices.text: You're late.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: So sorry about that.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: It took me quite some time to retrieve those Gardemeks he utilized without authorization. Well done, you didn't just break the rules, but also violated regulations.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Now it's your turn to accept your punishment. You're coming back with me.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: As for you guys... If you want to leave, this is your last chance. *sigh* With all the fuss he's been making, who knows what will happen later.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: Of course, it's also possible that nothing will happen at all.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: If you really want to thank me, don't come back again.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Then, with Estienne's help, the path is reopened...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon guesses we can go now... We should be in the clear now, right? Hm... Let's get a move on before we run into any more surprises!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: We're leaving Meropide again? Will we ever come back?

choices.text: Sure, if we do something bad out there.

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Oh, then...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Don't go running off causing trouble just to come back for a visit!

response.speaker: Lanoire
response.text: Well then, goodbye, Meropide.

choices.text: We'll use the front door next time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Going through the regular channels is safer.

choices.text: What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Estienne
response.text: "Atoning for my sins," of course.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You follow Estienne out of the Fortress of Meropide...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Together with Lanoire and Caterpillar, you carefully avoided detection by the evil sorcerers, and made it to safety...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Using shimmering magic to beat back the evil sorcerers, you made it to safety undetected...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Using shimmering magic to beat back the evil sorcerers, and later, with the help of the speaker, you made it to safety undetected...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You are escorted back to the Fortress of Meropide...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Should we try knocking?

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: ...Going somewhere?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You're not Estienne!

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: He had something to do, so he asked me to cover for him. *sigh*... When are people finally going to get it into their heads that I have my own work to do, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Th—Then can we leave?

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: You can... but it's dangerous out there. How dangerous, you ask? About as dangerous as the mental state of the new guard, I'd say...

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: He really is a lunatic. I had no idea that there were so many Gardemeks on the move! Not only that, people actually approve of his methods... Not that I know how serious those people are.

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: If you want to go, you'd better be prepared... I mean, it would be best if you didn't come back again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Lanoire's not back yet...

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: I'm here! Mr. Maupoil just brought me back.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Then there's no time to lose. Lanoire, I know we lost the last game to the evil sorcerer, but are you ready for a new challenge?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: A new game? You mean a new adventure? I'm ready! We can't let the evil sorcerer catch us again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Looks like they're all good. Are you ready then, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm sorry for dragging you two into this. My plan was to get Lanoire home to her family, then return on my own. But it looks like that plan was a complete failure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's a lot I want to ask you.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I imagine so.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... You really are Caterpillar, right?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I am.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, um, you're a Hilichurl?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I am.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But.... aren't Hilichurls all, um, kinda dumb? And you looked just like a regular kid before. Ugh... Paimon doesn't know what's real anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You said before that you looked like this because you got sick, after all, everyone has things they'd rather not tell anyone... And you're also so good to Lanoire, and she trusts you too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you're not a human at all... If you're a Hilichurl...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Then you can't trust me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I want the answers to the questions Noailles asked before.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'll answer all your questions truthfully.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: When did you come to the Fortress of Meropide?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Over 400 years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: F—Four hundred years ago!? When you said you'd been here a long time, Paimon thought you meant something like three to five years...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But 400 years is, like, several generations, isn't it? Oh, right... You're a Hilichurl...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What was your crime?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If you're interested in history... I was a member of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. I was found guilty of being an accessory to the master's scheme.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo... We've heard of that before!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm surprised anyone still remembers it...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The prophecy of the apocalypse... My master believed that he could stop this future of destruction from coming to pass. We did much to prepare for this. It was a powerful magic, and also an evil plan...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But perhaps none of this is important now. The plan failed, and the Narzissenkreuz Ordo has essentially ceased to exist. Whether Fontaine is destroyed or not, it no longer has anything to do with me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just who was this master you spoke of?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Narzissenkreuz, a powerful mage. He taught me human speech and granted me memory and intelligence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was there really someone who could do something like that? Hmm... But, your appearance aside, you really do seem like an ordinary human...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Though many details of the past have faded into memory, I remember this very well...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: This was a very, very long time ago. I couldn't change how I appeared to others at will then.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Many humans — some in finery, others in rags, some with curiosity, others with disdain — would all ask similar questions.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: "Can Hilichurls really talk?" "Are Hilichurls really capable of intelligence?"

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: My master raised the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz high. It was a ceremonial sword, so the blade wasn't sharp, but still it glistened in the sunlight.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: "Behold," he said, "even a hideous monster such as this can attain wisdom and redemption through my power as the incarnation of Narzissenkreuz."

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I was one of his creations. And as a testament to Narzissenkreuz's power, I once wielded a blade for the Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: But the sacred sword evidently couldn't save my master from a fate of failure and ruin. And the mystical, magical weapon... no longer exists.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: And there will be no more monsters in human skin like me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do you want to help Lanoire?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Because of "compassion"...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Humanity might be unattainable for me, but at the very least, I can imitate it. Just like how I learned to change how I appear to others.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't get it...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you both innately possess kindness and benevolence. Because of this, you don't need to think twice about helping others. You simply do.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: If you look at their outcomes alone, plenty of actions are indistinguishable from each other. We all agree that Lanoire shouldn't stay in the Fortress Meropide and that she should return to her family, so we chose to help her.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Your actions come from an innate benevolence that doesn't require excessive consideration or calculation. For me, however... it is because by doing so, I will be more like a human.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Funny, isn't it? I'll never truly become human, yet I can't stop mimicking human behavior.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's like "atonement"... As far as human law is concerned, I've long since atoned for my sins. But a human... What would a true human do?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: They would never forgive themselves for the mistakes they made, the harm they caused, and the people or things they failed to save...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: So, my sins can never be absolved, and I will forever be my own prisoner.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you plan to do next?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'll bring Lanoire back to her family.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But... Forget about getting out of the Fortress, we can't even get past this door!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I made a promise to her... so I have to fulfill it. She shouldn't stay here any longer, especially not by my side.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The Geode Mine Shaft... It's a dangerous route, but it's feasible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Geode Mine Shaft... That's right, Clynes said that there's an opening there that leads outside...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, the guards asked him to install a locking mechanism like the one at the Rift of Erosion.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He also said something about having prepared a "surprise"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes, there's no way that's anything good! Are you sure you want to go from there? Paimon seems to remember that the research terminal there has to be operated by two people at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Lanoire's so small, Paimon doesn't think she'll be able to operate it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Why don't we help them, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: I do innately possess kindness, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have a few more questions about the Ordo, as well...

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: I think there are other places better suited to discussing the history of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. Somewhere that isn't the Fortress of Meropide, for example.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then we'll just have to wait until after Lanoire is reunited with her family... Before any of that, we need to think of a way out of here. And we need to meet back up with Lanoire.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Estienne will help us open the door. But there's a limit to how much he can help us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He should be at the entrance, right? Let's go ask him!

choices.text: I'll do it for you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Where's Estienne?

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: He had something to do, so he asked me to cover for him. *sigh*... When are people finally going to get it into their heads that I have my own work to do, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Th—Then can we...

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: You want to get Lanoire out of here, right? It's not that you can't...

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: But it's dangerous out there. How dangerous, you ask? About as dangerous as the mental state of the new guard, I'd say...

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: He really is a lunatic. I had no idea that there were so many Gardemeks on the move! Not only that, people actually approve of his methods... Not that I know how serious those people are.

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: If you want to go, you'd better be prepared... I mean, it would be best if you didn't come back again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it! But... more importantly, where's Lanoire?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: I'm here! Mr. Maupoil just brought me back.

dialogues.speaker: Maupoil
dialogues.text: That's right. The thoughtful, considerate Maupoil brought her back while he was covering for Estienne.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Thank you, thoughtful and considerate Mr. Maupoil!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Then there's no time to lose. Lanoire, I know we lost the last game to the evil sorcerer, but are you ready for a new challenge?

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: A new game? You mean a new adventure? I'm ready! We can't let the evil sorcerer catch us again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Looks like they're all good. Are you ready then, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: Natural wind really feels better, doesn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: We might have fans down there, but most of the air feels kind of stale.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: The fans in the Pankration Ring are just like Noailles. The fans are indeed needed there, but when their blades spin, they bring the same misery to everyone no matter who they are.

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: I think you know what I'm talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #I'll be rooting for you, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: We'll take care of things here.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Let's ask the guards first.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Now that Lanoire's back, we can set off at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: #A new adventure... I'm ready! Let's go, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}. We won't lose to the evil sorcerer this time!

dialogues.speaker: Estienne
dialogues.text: If you're looking for Caterpillar, he's inside. As for Lanoire, she'll be back after she finishes filling out her registration form.
